standard_prerequisites.use: Smoothness at a point, small extensions of local rings, and the schemes-side Artinian lifting criterion; the reduction is retained.

core_obligations: Pass to an etale chart making the point an ordinary point of a scheme, and apply the schemes-side Artinian lifting criterion there.
Show that testing only small extensions suffices, by reducing an arbitrary square-zero surjection of local rings to that case.

proof_roadmap.step: Choose an etale chart and relocate the point to a scheme.
Apply the schemes-side lifting criterion at that point.
Reduce the general test class to small extensions.

difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises smoothness at a point of a morphism of algebraic spaces by a lifting property against surjections of local rings with square-zero kernel, and shows that it suffices to test small extensions. The proof passes to an etale chart so that the point becomes an ordinary point of a scheme, applies the schemes-side lifting criterion there, and then transports the conclusion back; the restriction to small extensions follows from a standard reduction on the test algebras. Passing the pointwise lifting condition through the chart is the load-bearing step. Retained author proof at lines 5119-5160.

dedup.scope: Cross-chapter same-name pair. The A side is stated for morphisms of schemes with S locally Noetherian and lists four equivalent conditions; this side is stated for morphisms of algebraic spaces, works at a point, and lists three. The statements are not identical and the listings differ, so under the Lead's rule they are distinct propositions and both are counted; this card records the algebraic-spaces side. Compared against all focused-seeds task.json, PREPARATION_WORKLIST.jsonl, and public intervals for spaces-more-morphisms.tex.

compared.difference: Hypothesis difference: the A side assumes a morphism of schemes with a locally Noetherian base and tests at a point of the source; this side assumes a morphism of algebraic spaces and works at a point of the underlying topological space. Conclusion difference: the A side lists four equivalent conditions including a small-extension form with a residue-field condition, this side three, so the two statements differ and both count.
